rows: Arrow: no, inherits from surrounding scope

blocks.text: Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values passed at the call. JavaScript never checks the count: missing arguments become undefined, extra ones are ignored.
Default values are evaluated at call time, on every call. function f(list = []) gives each call a fresh array, unlike Python's shared mutable default.
Keep the returned expression on the same line as return. A line break right after return makes the function return undefined.
Passing Objects: Mutation Is Visible, Reassignment Is Not

Everything is passed by value, but for objects that value is a reference ("call by sharing"). A function without side effects that always returns the same output for the same input is a pure function: easier to test, reuse and debug.
